question: Explain Java garbage collection and different GC algorithms. How would you tune GC for a high-throughput vs low-latency application?

keyPoints: GC algorithms: Serial (single-threaded), Parallel (throughput), CMS (low pause), G1 (balanced), ZGC/Shenandoah (ultra-low latency)
High-throughput: use Parallel GC, larger heap, longer pause times acceptable
Low-latency: use G1/ZGC, tune for shorter pause times, may sacrifice some throughput
Key metrics: GC pause duration, frequency, throughput percentage
Tune heap size (-Xms/-Xmx), young/old generation ratio, GC threads
expectedAnswer.codeExample:
// GC tuning examples

// High-throughput batch processing
java -Xms4g -Xmx4g \
  -XX:+UseParallelGC \
  -XX:ParallelGCThreads=8 \
  -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=1000 \
  -jar app.jar

// Low-latency web application  
java -Xms4g -Xmx4g \
  -XX:+UseG1GC \
  -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200 \
  -XX:G1ReservePercent=10 \
  -XX:InitiatingHeapOccupancyPercent=45 \
  -jar app.jar

// Ultra-low latency (Java 11+)
java -Xms4g -Xmx4g \
  -XX:+UseZGC \
  -XX:ZCollectionInterval=5 \
  -jar app.jar
expectedAnswer.explanation: GC choice depends on application requirements. High-throughput applications (batch processing, analytics) benefit from Parallel GC which maximizes CPU utilization but may have longer pause times (100ms+). Low-latency applications (real-time APIs, trading systems) need G1 or ZGC to keep pauses under 10-200ms. G1GC divides heap into regions, does concurrent marking, and predicts pause times. ZGC/Shenandoah achieve sub-10ms pauses through concurrent compaction. Monitor with -XX:+PrintGCDetails, use GC logs to identify issues: frequent full GCs indicate undersized heap, long pauses suggest wrong collector.
